title: U.S. House · South Dakota At-Large
area: Statewide, South Dakota (single at-large congressional district).

context.text: Open seat: incumbent Dusty Johnson (R) is not seeking re-election to the House and withdrew from this race, running instead for Governor of South Dakota in 2026. Marty Jackley, the sitting South Dakota Attorney General, defeated James Bialota 79.2%-20.8% in the June 2, 2026 Republican primary (Casey Crabtree and Dusty Johnson also withdrew from that primary). Nicole Gronli (also known as Nikki Gronli) advanced unopposed after South Dakota's Democratic primary was canceled. Jack Pittman (independent) did not make the general-election ballot.

candidates.name: Marty Jackley
candidates.currentRole: Attorney General of South Dakota (2023-present; previously 2009-2019)

priorities.text: Public safety: backing police, sheriffs and prosecutors, drawing on his career prosecuting violent crime as Attorney General.
Border and immigration: securing the border and "finishing the wall," citing his prosecution of drug traffickers.
Supporting the Trump administration's agenda, including securing the border and cutting taxes.

candidates.researchNotes: Two earlier entries (guns, immigration_enforcement) were removed because the issues page only says he supports the Second Amendment and "secure the border, finish the wall," which are general statements. At the Oct. 1, 2026 debate he described support for "targeted tariffs" on China and opposed the Argentine beef import plan; no position was recorded for broad tariffs or health coverage.

statements.quote: We need to make sure, with respect to targeted tariffs, that we're doing everything we can to promote American jobs and to get our products a fair deal and a fair trade
statements.context: In the Oct. 1, 2026 debate, per South Dakota Searchlight

candidates.name: Nicole Gronli

priorities.text: Says she is running to advocate for South Dakota and build "an economy that works for everyone."

positions.summary: At the Oct. 1, 2026 debate she criticized the Trump administration's tariffs, including those on Canada, and in an August press release criticized 50% tariffs on Canadian products.
positions.quote: All Americans are suffering under the tariffs

candidates.researchNotes: Gronli's campaign site has no issues page (a linked "Priorities" page returned a 404); positions are drawn from her campaign blog posts and press releases and the Oct. 1, 2026 debate coverage. Her statements on abortion and child care were general and not recorded as positions.

statements.quote: People aren’t going to have access to health insurance
statements.context: In the Oct. 1, 2026 debate, on the Medicaid changes in the 2025 budget law, per South Dakota Searchlight
